{{Quote|Behold the vengeful remains of Rur, High Shaman of the Order of the Terrible Glare!|Rur|<ref name="BF" />}}
The '''Order of the Terrible Glare''' was a splinter group of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], formed by dissident [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] during the [[Pius Dea Crusades]]. When the Jedi Order [[Recusal|recused]] itself from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during this time, these dissenters rallied to the [[Pius Dea]] cause, and abandoned [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] in favor of [[Garn/Legends|Garn]]. Becoming a violent and dangerous cult led by [[Shaman/Legends|shamans]], the Order waged war against the Jedi before being destroyed at the end of the Crusades. The sole survivor, [[Rur/Legends|Rur]], lived on in a [[Computer/Legends|computer]] and lured Jedi to Garn for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]], taking vengeance on them one at a time. However, Rur was finally [[Mission to Garn|defeated]] by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], which brought an end to this ancient Order.

==Description==
{{Quote|My mind was encoded and preserved within the devices of knowing you see before you.|Rur|<ref name="BF" />}}
Originally a splinter group of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] formed during the Order's [[Recusal]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Pius Dea Crusades]], the Order of the Terrible Glare was descended from [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who had embraced the [[Pius Dea]] cult's brand of violent [[Humanocentrism]].<ref name="EGTW" /> Led by a [[High Shaman of the Terrible Glare|High Shaman]], the Order of the Terrible Glare was driven by its hatred of the Jedi Order<ref name="BF" /> it was once a part of,<ref name="EGTW" /> and made use of novel technologies in its battles with the Jedi&mdash;including [[Computer/Legends|computer]] systems capable of preserving the consciousness of a deceased person, and crystal prisms called [[soul snare]]s that could indefinitely imprison the soul of a being.<ref name="BF" />

==History==
{{Quote|The Terrible... of course! The Order of the Terrible Glare once fought a monstrous war with the Jedi Knights. Ben told me about it. The Jedi won, of course. They wiped the Order out and laid waste to their homeworld, Garn. This world...|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="BF" />}}
[[File:Garn.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The desolate world of Garn.]]
The Order of the Terrible Glare was a group of dissident [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] who splintered from the Jedi Order when the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] withdrew to [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] during the Pius Dea Crusades of the Galactic Republic. Believing that the Pius Dea were correct in their pursuit, these Jedi abandoned the Order and championed the crusaders who were causing turmoil across the Republic.<ref name="EGTW" /> The [[Shaman/Legends|shamans]] of the Order developed soul snares&mdash;crystal prisms that were capable of imprisoning the life force of a sapient being for eternity. Master [[Mind trick/Legends|illusionists]], the shamans of the Order of the Terrible Glare established a base on the desolate [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Garn/Legends|Garn]], where they stored massive computer terminals to store their knowledge and equipped with sensors able to detect [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] across interstellar distances.<ref name="BF" /> At some point, the Order also allied with a race of inter-dimensional monsters known as the [[Rozzum]].<ref name="{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-1|text=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire, Part 1|int=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire}}">''{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-1|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>

Despite the length of the Crusades and the fanaticism of the Order's shamans, the Jedi Order proved to be more powerful and were able to overthrow Pius Dea-aligned [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Contispex XIX]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. With the Republic under control, the Jedi Order dispatched a strike team to Garn and laid waste to the world.<ref name="EGTW" /> While all members of the Order were thought to have been killed, High Shaman [[Rur/Legends|Rur]] survived long enough to encode and preserve his mind within one of the Order's computers. Trapped within the Order's black tower, Rur would secretly continue to wage war against the Jedi Order for millennia, using long-range sensors to detect [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] and sending false distress signals to lure their wielders to Garn and to their [[Death/Legends|deaths]]. Rur, in his computerized state, lost sense of [[Time/Legends|time]]; a span of more than 10,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] was to him but a few months.<ref name="BF" />

At the height of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Rur [[Mission to Garn|lured]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to Garn using a distress signal in which a woman pleaded for help from his tower. There, Skywalker was "attacked" by giant "pale squirmers," manifestations of his own fears, and discovered soul-snares still containing the life forces of fallen Jedi Knights. Elsewhere in the tower, he discovered the desiccated skeletal remains of armored Jedi, and ancient and alien remains unknown to him.<ref name="BF" />

[[File:Rur.jpg|thumb|right|200px|High Shaman Rur.]]

Ultimately, Skywalker encountered the vengeful remains of Rur, who appeared as a green-skinned humanoid figure draped in ornate vestments within a green translucent pyramid. Rur accused the Jedi of treachery in their "recent" attack "many months ago," and announced his intention to take revenge on Skywalker as he had done to so many others. Recognizing the planet and the ancient Order from a story briefly related to him by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Skywalker explained to Rur that the Jedi were all dead, killed in the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], and that he was not a Jedi, but merely a man with a lightsaber. Unable to reconcile the destruction of the Jedi Order and the passage of so much time with his ancient lust for revenge, Rur fell into a self-destructive fit of dissonance, and destroyed the tower. Skywalker narrowly escaped, reflecting on the hatred and vengeful spirit that had finally consumed the last of the shamans of the Order of the Terrible Glare.<ref name="BF" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Order of the Terrible Glare was introduced in "[[Blind Fury!]]," a [[1982]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] story appearing in [[Star Wars Monthly 159|''Star Wars Monthly'' 159]], written by [[Alan Moore]] and illustrated by [[John Stokes]].<ref name="BF" />
